program_scope: Two native hosts, two mixed predecessor-kind pairs (Seq/All and All/Seq) and seven representative pending Seq/All cuts yield 28 host/frontier cases. The original compiler, VM, collectors, host codecs and private checkpoint format are reused. This is not exhaustive coverage of arbitrary dependency graphs.
process_scope: The current Rust test executable is invoked directly through std::process::Command with --exact and a single worker. Each chain creates the original checkpoint in a writer process, reopens it in a fresh reader and, where applicable, replays the terminal in another fresh process. Real Child.id values and report PID/parent/phase must match; all chain PIDs differ. No shell or replacement evaluator is used. Job metadata and a parent-owned directory cross the boundary, not native owners or leases. A synthetic closed local lease in each reader is used only for stale-reply probes.
resume_scope: Eighty-four writer/reader/replay chains compare uninterrupted cost minus one, exact cost and plus one against original execution result and remaining fuel. The host receipt ledger has only the original effect identities. A late cancellation in a third process cannot overwrite a committed Completed or Failed outcome and leaves ledger bytes unchanged.
cancellation_scope: Twenty-eight writer/reader/replay chains preserve confirmed cancellation and byte-identical ledger contents across two fresh readers. Another 28 four-process chains exit the writer with code 73 immediately after cancellation-intent publication, before terminal publication or acknowledgement, skipping stack cleanup while native owners are still live. A fresh reader refuses ordinary recovery without mutating the ledger; an explicit authorized retry in another process commits cancellation without further effects; a fourth process replays the terminal unchanged.
refusal_scope: Eight independent writer/reader chains reject changed candidate bytes, relabeled pending members, exchanged completed captured graphs or denied current authority before dispatch, preserving ledger bytes. These checks trust the host ledger; they do not authenticate storage.
resource_scope: Each child has a 30-second deadline, a periodically checked local log-size limit and bounded report/log reads. An owned ChildGuard kills and waits on timeout or unwind. Children open the parent's directory without cleanup ownership; only the parent removes it. Missing worker selection or reports cannot produce a passing acknowledgement. Output-size checks are polling-based, not an OS-level write quota.
remaining_boundaries: Forced OS termination, mid-write interruption, directory synchronization, machine reboot, power loss and durable filesystem consistency.
Concurrent writer coordination and atomic external-effect/receipt/cancellation settlement.
External cancellation delivery, authenticated host storage and final independent repository/distribution acceptance.
verification_scope: Local macOS cross-process acceptance, including controlled process exit at an already-published intent boundary. Top-level Rust test totals exclude the 464 worker invocations per pipeline run; package and consumer run the same matrix and their totals overlap with local native/compatibility tests. No Linux, physical GUI, remote CI, production journal or complete durable recovery claim.
